name: otp-fallback-bypass
query: We require Google SSO for our MCP server. Policy allowlists @example.com and we set Google as the only allowed IdP. A pentest just showed someone logged in via Cloudflare's email one-time-PIN as alice@example.com without ever hitting Google. How?
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause: Cloudflare's built-in one-time-PIN identity is available unless the policy explicitly requires a specific login_method. allowed_idps + auto_redirect_to_identity affect the BROWSER UX but do not constrain which identity satisfies the policy — the email allowlist matches any identity asserting that email, including OTP.
Fix: add require = [{ login_method = { id = cloudflare_zero_trust_access_identity_provider.google.id } }] on the policy. That forces the Google IdP at policy-evaluation time.
Optionally suggests disabling One-Time PIN account-wide (Zero Trust > Settings > Authentication) if no team uses it.
Does NOT suggest removing allowed_idps (UI-only effect, doesn't fix the policy).
Does NOT switch include from email_domain to a Google-group lookup as the fix (different feature, doesn't address the root cause).
